implementation_by_plan_point.summary: Two public zero-argument operations dayz_knowledge_status and dayz_knowledge_prepare registered via FastMCP; no path/URL/repo/credential parameters. M22 owns server.py schema/wire; verified read-only that server.py registers the tools and that the frozen arrays in test_effective_schema_catalog.py already contain both names plus dayz_effective_schema.

dayz_knowledge_status is read-only and publishes independent index_state/pack_state each in missing|invalid|valid, can_query=(index_state==valid), can_prepare=(pack_state==valid), effective paths, and bounded reason enums.
dayz_knowledge_prepare calls only knowledge_pack.resolve_pack_dir() and extract_pack(); ensure_pack/git/network are never reachable from MCP (test asserts ensure_pack raises if called).

validate_index enforces non-empty list root, object entries with non-empty name/source_file strings, non-empty evidence list, and evidence items with non-empty path string and positive integer line (bool rejected); optional fields keep the extract_pack() schema; load_index wraps JSON/Unicode errors into KnowledgeIndexError.

Publication takes a persistent sibling anchor <index>.prepare.lock pinned as a regular non-reparse file, holds a non-blocking exclusive OS byte-range lock (msvcrt.locking LK_NBLCK, fail-closed as knowledge_prepare_conflict), generates one 32-hex txid, creates only <index>.candidate.<txid> via os.open with O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL(+O_BINARY) mode 0o600, serializes deterministically, fsyncs, re-reads and re-validates with the independent validator, then publishes via os.replace; each exit cleans only its own exact candidate; any failure before replace leaves the previous index byte-identical.

dayz_knowledge_find/show kept with same names/arguments/result and now read the published index; descriptions and both failure codes carry the remedy 'call dayz_knowledge_status, then dayz_knowledge_prepare'; no host command/path remains in any public surface.

Nine-cell cartesian matrix with exact codes: find/show depend only on the index axis; prepare depends only on the pack axis; conflict and pack failures leave the index untouched; show keeps unknown_api on a valid index.

Functional pos/neg suite with {} calls: nine cells, legacy-style valid index, JSON/root/entry invalid mutants, empty extraction, extractor failure, replace failure, repeated deterministic prepare, find/show consume published index, two-process barrier (both arms) and lock hardening tests. No schema/list_tools/extras assertions before M22.

Added test_extract_pack_output_passes_the_strong_published_validator tying extract_pack output to validate_index (plan point 4).

verification_limitation: The project venv tools/.venv-mcp is Windows-only and this WSL session has no WSLInterop, so the Windows-native interpreter could not be executed from this session. Functional verification ran on a disposable Linux venv (Python 3.11.16) with an msvcrt shim mapping LK_NBLCK/LK_UNLCK onto POSIX fcntl record locks (per-process, non-blocking, OSError on contention) and fork-based two-process isolation. The real msvcrt.locking byte-range path should be re-run in the Windows native environment at the REVIEW gate; this is the single environment caveat for this hop.
